mutant.description: THE CLAIM MOST AT RISK OF BEING AN INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT IS PART 1's DISCRIMINATING CONTROL: 'FMT/FMTC appears in 0 of 7,341 eight-digit rows'. A NAME-MATCHER THAT WAS SIMPLY DEAD ON THE 8-DIGIT CLASS WOULD PRODUCE EXACTLY THAT ZERO, and the whole two-custodian finding would rest on a broken instrument -- the anti-correlation class where the cleaner the result, the more complete the failure. MUTATION RUN: hold the matcher, the class split and the corpus fixed and change ONLY the search token, to 'IRA' -- a token that MUST appear in both grammar classes if the matcher is alive on both. Plus a null token 'ZZQQXX' that must return 0 in both, so the matcher is shown to be discriminating rather than merely non-empty. THE CENTRAL RISK IN PART 2 IS THAT 'ABSENT FROM RECENT PARTITIONS' IS AN ARTIFACT OF THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A DEPARTURE -- a universe whose partitions vary in coverage would manufacture exactly the observation the contract calls a departure. I attacked that directly instead of trusting it. CONTROL 1 (POSITIVE, and it nearly inverted the reading): an account drawn FROM the 2026-08-18 universe, carried through the identical 540-partition read, appears in only 173 of 540 -- which looks like lossiness. Reading its SHAPE rather than its count settles it: it enters at 2025-12-19 and is present contiguously in every partition since, so the universe is an accumulating roster and absence after contiguous presence is a real exit. WITHOUT THIS CONTROL THE 161/379 SPLIT WOULD HAVE BEEN UNINTERPRETABLE. CONTROL 2 (MIGRATION / NEGATIVE): all 659 partitions of the sibling 49F scope schwab/08242234 tested for both accounts -- 0 of 659, so they did not move between books. CONTROL 3 (CLOSURE-EXPRESSIVENESS, the one that turns 'open' from an absence of modelling into a positive assertion): both lifecycle carriers were censused for their ability to say 'closed' -- dim_account.account_status_raw carries 188 'C' of 8,633, and the SmartX roster carries 2,498 'close' + 23 'workingClose' of 9,860. Both CAN express closure; both say open. CONTROL 4 (PART 1, TWO-SIDED): the FMT/FMTC registration claim is not scored on its own class alone -- the discriminating half is 0 of 7,341 eight-digit rows, and the reverse control is SCHWAB at 4,383 of 7,341 eight-digit vs 0 of 18 nine-digit. A one-sided count would have been a pattern; the disjointness in both directions is the finding. CONTROL 5 (WHICH UNIVERSE): the contract's own three denominators were re-derived against BOTH candidate 49F scopes to settle which universe was actually measured -- 532/7,316/7,305 reproduce against 08335338 and 651/7,240 against 08242234 do not, so the comment naming 08242234 is a doc error and the substance is sound. ADDITIONAL CONTROLS RUN AND REPORTED IN THE SAME PASS -- NEGATIVE/CALENDAR: TRADING CALENDAR RESOLVED BEFORE ANY STALENESS READING (NEVER#4): the 2026-08-29 allocation-map partition is 0 rows / 4,507 B, and a naive read would have called the feed broken. Enumerating the last 18 partitions with day-of-week shows every Sat/Sun at exactly 4,507 B and 0 rows (08-15, 08-16, 08-22, 08-23, 08-29) against 7,264-7,359 rows on business days -- the established weekend shape. Friday 2026-08-28 is the live vintage and every 'today' number is read there. A second empty-read trap was caught the same way: fact_account_detail's 2026-08-28 partition is empty, and rather than concluding 'no custodian data exists' the full 46-partition size profile was enumerated, finding exactly one populated partition (2026-07-14) -- which is a NULL RESULT WITH A DENOMINATOR (0 of 13 keys present in 91 rows), not an absence. GRAIN: GRAIN CHECKED BEFORE THE CLAIM, AND IT CHANGED THE ANSWER TWICE. (1) The residual is an ALLOCATION-ROW-grain object; 'does anything count them' is a question about SERVED ARTIFACTS, so it was answered by scanning artifacts (23 gold tables, every column) rather than by reading consumer code -- code-reading would have found b04 'carries residual rows' and stopped, missing that b04 has never emitted. (2) The served AUM plane is MODEL-grain and vendor-computed, so it cannot answer an account-grain question at all; that grain mismatch is why the channel is reported UNDECIDABLE rather than assumed either way.
